Hi, I'm Marcos 👋

Senior Software Engineer, Release & Reliability at Nethermind, based in Buenos Aires.

I run releases for the Nethermind execution client. Nothing reaches node operators until it has passed our soak fleets on mainnet, Gnosis, Sepolia, Hoodi and OP networks. Most days that means:

  • Release engineering: release branches, backports, smoke-test triage, and separating real client bugs from CI noise.
  • Test infrastructure: Terraform-managed node fleets on GCP, self-hosted CI runners, and Prometheus/Loki dashboards with alerts for stalls and memory.
  • Fork days: live monitoring of every node's health and chain agreement during network upgrades.
  • Client fixes: sync, pruning, txpool, networking and JSON-RPC hardening.
  • AI tooling for the team: LLM pull-request review in CI, and routing CI failures to the engineer responsible.

Before that I was one of the first engineers on Juno, Nethermind's Starknet full node in Go, and I've worked on Sedge, a one-command node and validator setup tool.

Public numbers: 118 merged PRs in nethermind, 104 in sedge and 32 in juno, plus 250+ PR reviews in nethermind.

On my own time: Payverge, an open-source restaurant operating system in Go and Next.js, and small developer tools such as grok-in-codex.

What I enjoy most is taking a complex technical idea, digging into it until it feels simple, and then distilling it into something minimal, visual, and interactive that makes it click for others too.

That's the thread running through most of my open-source 🚀 projects: algorithms and data structures in JavaScript, machine learning built from scratch, a neural network in a handful of functions, a self-parking car that learns through a genetic algorithm, and more.

I also write 📝 articles about learning, life, web development, and machine learning. My work has been featured in Hacker News, TechCrunch, JavaScript Weekly, Wikipedia, and MDN (publications).
